segments.text: Good morning. I am at a breakfast stall near Yongkang Street.
The owner has been frying scallion pancakes here since five in the morning.
This one is filled with egg and a little bit of sweet soy sauce.
If you come later than nine, the sesame flatbread is usually gone.
She says the dough rests overnight so it stays flaky, not tough.
I will take one pancake and a cup of hot soy milk, unsweetened.
The soy milk is freshly ground. You can smell the beans from the street.
That is breakfast in Taipei: hot, fast, and gone by midmorning.
